newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen opens flood relief forum, calls for aid.
newsitem.headline: Yemen opens flood relief forum, calls for aid.

text.p: Yemen inaugurated a donor's forum on Saturday in support of a national flood relief programme launched after torrential rains in June killed more than 300 people and caused $1.2 billion in damages.

"On behalf of the Yemeni government I call on all participants of this meeting to tell your governments about the impact of the floods and the extent of the disaster," Yemen's Prime Minister Abdul-Aziz Abdul-Ghani told delegates at the meeting of donor representatives.

A United Nations official working in Sanaa told Reuters the two-day meeting had been organised by Yemen's ministry of planning and development in coordination with the United Nations, the Dutch government and the World Bank.

"The meeting's goal is to mobilise technical and material assistance from the traditional donors and to call on new donors and parties from east Asia, Scandinavia and Canada to help Yemen overcome the consequences of this disaster," he said.
Representatives from 55 countries in addition to 12 regional and international organisations are participating in the meeting.
Following the floods -- the worst seen in the impoverished Arab country for three decades -- Yemen issued an international appeal for emergency aid.

A number of countries in the Middle East, North America and Asia provided food supplies, medicine, blankets and tents. The United Nations estimated the cost of this assistance at more than $10 million.
The torrential rains killed about 340 people and caused $1.2 billion in damages. Hundreds of others died from disease, mostly malaria, after the floods.
